deviations.what: Graded governor on the Spark cortex: the target container gains explicit GPU device nodes (devices: /dev/nvidia0, /dev/nvidiactl, /dev/nvidia-modeset, /dev/nvidia-uvm, /dev/nvidia-uvm-tools) in docker-compose.override.yml so docker update no longer revokes GPU access, and the governor runs with bands raised for this Spark's acpitz zones (cap 12 cpus at >=92 C, 8 at >=95 C, 4 at >=98 C, pause at >=101 C) instead of the 84/88/91/93.5 defaults
deviations.reason: The governor's first docker update killed the cortex lane's first boot with NVMLError_Unknown (systemd cgroup driver revokes NEW GPU access on docker update; reproduced on a throwaway container; explicit --device entries verified to survive docker update --cpus 8/4/12/16), and this Spark's acpitz zones idle ~88 C and reach 92 C under one benchmark stream, so the default bands would throttle at idle (docs/evidence/2026-10-17-accept-vllm-031-spark-cortex.txt)

deviations.what: Split engine pin: Thor and Orin stay on vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0-ubuntu2404; the Spark's cortex is tested on v0.30.0-ubuntu2404 (index sha256:439c19d48db36401abc914b9842d060fe610a54bc3ac29bb02505f0b69af1baf) and spark2 does not move to 0.31.0 until strict+thinking is clean there
deviations.reason: On 0.31.0 (xgrammar 0.2.7, both the plain and -ubuntu2404 variants) a strict tool call WITH thinking on the cortex lane emits 78 repeated calls until max_tokens; the nightly (xgrammar 0.2.3) emits one call. The structural-tag grammar is identical across engines, so the runtime enforcement regressed.
